fan's seam now runs both halves in the forced order: fan_verify
explores meaning-space by forking (candidates conflict, each proves in
its own rolled-back branch cursor, proof is a filter), then

mentl/2721609:
A Mentl program prints "Hello, kernel!" to the shell. The medium
speaks at fd_write resolution. Five substrate-bug closures land
together, each at its read-site per
protocol_emit_is_graph_projection.md.

Verified end-to-end:

  $ cat tutorial.mn | mentl ... | wat2wasm | wasmtime
  Hello, kernel!

Substrate landings (atomic):

1. Hβ.emit.memory-effect-op-direct-emit: Memory-effect ops
   (load_i32, load_i8, store_i32, store_i8) emit RAW WASM
   instructions instead of routing through the polymorphic-
   perform band-aid. Lower-side $memory_op_target_name dispatches
   on op_name to "memory_<op>" target; emit-side
   $emit_lperform's "memory_" prefix branch emits raw
   `(i32.load offset=0)` / `(i32.store offset=0)` /
   `(i32.load8_u offset=0)` / `(i32.store8 offset=0)` byte
   sequences.

   Stores follow `(i32.const 0)` unit-sentinel so let-bindings
   `let _ = perform store_i32(...)` have a value to consume —
   Mentl semantics is `() -> Int` boxed-as-i32; WASM i32.store
   returns nothing.

2. Hβ.first-light.string-data-segment-len-prefix: emit's
   $emit_string_section was emitting only payload bytes,
   dropping the `[len:i32]` prefix that Mentl's string convention
   requires. Runtime `load_i32(s)` read the first 4 payload
   bytes as length — nonsense values (e.g., 1.8 GB for "Hello").
   Fixed by emitting the entire string (4-byte length-prefix +
   payload).

   This was the FINAL substrate-bug between "compiles clean" and
   "actually prints." fd_write was returning errno 48 because the
   iov length was the first 4 payload bytes interpreted as i32
   instead of the actual string length.

mentl/270d72c:
Per MV-LSP-adapter walkthrough §1 (commit 4d0fce1). The first sub-handle
of the MV-LSP arc — reusable JSON substrate that bridges raw bytes
and Inka-native ADTs. Reusable beyond LSP (web playground, MCP,
debug adapter all compose on the same substrate).

JsonValue ADT — six variants matching JSON spec:
  JNull / JBool(Bool) / JNum(Float) / JStr(String) / JArr(List) / JObj(List)

JObj fields are List<(String, JsonValue)> tuples per Insight #9
(records-as-handler-state-shape) — order-preserving (LSP capability
negotiation depends on key order in some clients), lookup via linear
scan (LSP messages are small).

JsonResult ADT — JOk(value, pos) | JErr(msg, pos). Per drift mode 9:
no silent absorption of parse errors. Caller pattern-matches; LSP
session loop reports JErr to the protocol; library callers handle
recovery as they choose.

Parser — recursive descent, position-threading, cons-then-reverse for
arrays/objects. ~280 lines. Honest scope:
  - Strings: \, ", \n, \r, \t, \b, \f, \/ escapes; \uXXXX deferred
    to JSON.unicode peer (rare in LSP traffic; ASCII covers common path)
  - Numbers: integer + decimal forms parsed as Float (JNum carries
    Float; LSP integer fields cast at use site via float_to_int_truncate)
  - Whitespace: space / tab / newline / CR per spec

Serializer — canonical formatting (no extra whitespace, no trailing
newlines). Object keys appear in JObj list order. String escaping
covers the symmetric set of parser-recognized escapes.

Lookup helpers (consumed by lsp_adapter):
  json_obj_get(v, key) -> Option<JsonValue>     — linear scan; H6 over JsonValue
  json_str_or_default(v, default) -> String     — extract or fallback
  json_int_or_default(v, default) -> Int        — extract Int via truncate

Eight interrogations:
  Graph?    N/A; data substrate (no graph reads)
  Handler?  N/A; pure parse/serialize fns
  Verb?     recursive descent; flat let/match (no pipe topology forced)
  Row?      with Memory + Alloc (string traversal + ADT alloc)

clob/271ab2a:
The single fire-and-forget script for the first real run. Everything end to
end: acquire -> tokenize -> synth -> calibrate-confidence(+meta) ->
train-router -> ingest (checkpointed) -> crystal -> bench-suite (ablation on
the held-out split) -> metrics summary.

Built to be left running on an idle machine:
- best-effort renice/ionice-idle on self so clob yields if anything wakes;
  non-fatal if the kernel denies it (runs at normal priority instead).
- set -euo pipefail, tee to <experiment>/run.log (survives `nohup ... &`),
  per-step wall-clock, and a clear DONE/FAILED banner naming the failed step.
- ingest checkpoints every 50k tokens, so a crash mid-run is resumable.
- pre-flight vocab guard (BPE merges vs model vocab) aborts before the long
  run rather than dying mid-stream.

SMOKE=1 runs the whole chain on the in-repo corpus in ~30s (validated end to
end) and doubles as Phase N's smoke_test. Tunables via env: SEED, CONFIG
(seed|small|tiny), N_MERGES, MAX_TOKENS (0=all), EPOCHS, EXPERIMENT_NAME,
NICE. Corpus overrides (CORPUS_NAME/CORPUS_URL) pass through to
acquire_corpus.sh.

Note: this run trains the heads/router and crystallizes modules; the ternary
core stays at synth init (the architecture as built). It is the first
real-data test of Bet 2, not core-weight training.

perennials/27f30f7:
Hardiness. zoneOk excludes a plant with no record exactly as it excludes one
that would die there, and 2,788 of the 8,800 have no record -- so "hardy in
zone 6, 3,730 plants" reads as a claim about survival when most of the
exclusions are a claim about paperwork. The rail says so, once she sets a zone.
useZone() is deleted rather than wired: it had no call sites, and defaulting a
zone would have fired that exclusion silently on every cold open.

Undo. Constraint edits replace the history entry instead of pushing one, so the
browser's Back cannot take back a wipe. "clear" and removing a trail step now
keep what they destroyed and offer it back.

Cold start. The name index took an 8,800-document pass on the main thread on
every cold launch -- including a fully offline one in the garden, where the
service worker hands over the bytes instantly and the phone then freezes for
half a second anyway. It is needed only when she types a name. Build it when
the browser next goes idle, and on the spot if she types first.

Adding a constraint no longer wipes an active text search, which used to drop
the text step out of the trail and make the results grow. The filter bar is
sticky, so changing a constraint forty plants deep no longer means flicking
back to the top one-handed. And the loading gate says what it is downloading,
how big it is, and that it happens once.
